subject: Sir2 (yeast)
context: Sir2 (silent information regulator 2) is the founding member of the sirtuin family, first identified in Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a regulator of mating-type locus silencing and replicative lifespan. The seven mammalian paralogues SIRT1–SIRT7 evolved from this ancestral NAD+-dependent deacetylase, retaining the conserved catalytic core while diversifying in subcellular localization and substrate repertoire. This phylogenetic continuity means insights from yeast Sir2 historically informed mammalian sirtuin biology, although the mammalian enzymes acquired lineage-specific regulatory domains. The relationship is directional: yeast Sir2 is the evolutionary precursor, not a downstream effector, of the SIRT1–7 family.

subject: Sirtuins
context: Sirtuins are class III histone deacetylases whose catalytic mechanism absolutely requires NAD+ as a co-substrate, coupling deacetylation to the cellular redox and energy state. Each turnover hydrolyzes one NAD+ molecule into nicotinamide and 2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose while removing an acetyl group from a lysine residue on the target protein. This strict NAD+ dependence means sirtuin activity rises when the NAD+/NADH ratio is high, as occurs during caloric restriction, exercise, or fasting, and falls when NAD+ is depleted. A caveat is that this dependency creates competition with other NAD+-consuming enzymes such as CD38 and PARPs for the same limited co-substrate pool.

subject: Sirtuins
context: Beyond deacetylation, several sirtuins catalyze mono-ADP-ribosylation, transferring the ADP-ribose moiety of NAD+ onto target proteins without removing an acetyl group. SIRT4 and SIRT6 prominently display this mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity, with SIRT6 using it to recruit heterochromatin proteins such as KAP1/HP1α. The directionality is that NAD+ is the donor and the target lysine (or other residue) is the acceptor, producing a mono-ADP-ribosylated product rather than free OAADPr. Biologically, ADP-ribosylation allows sirtuins to regulate processes—such as DNA repair and LINE-1 repression—distinct from their deacetylase functions.

subject: Sirtuin deacetylation reaction
context: During the sirtuin-catalyzed deacetylation of a lysine, NAD+ is cleaved between its nicotinamide and ADP-ribose moieties, and the acetyl group is transferred to the ADP-ribose to generate 2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose (OAADPr) plus free nicotinamide. OAADPr is a stoichiometric by-product, released in equimolar amounts with the deacetylated substrate on every catalytic cycle. This molecule is not merely waste: it binds and activates the TRPM2 cation channel, linking sirtuin activity to calcium signaling and cellular stress responses. A caveat is that OAADPr accumulation can itself feed back on cellular metabolism, and its levels reflect the integrated deacetylase flux of the cell.

subject: OAADPr
context: OAADPr (2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose) binds to the cytoplasmic N-terminal domain of the TRPM2 non-selective cation channel, promoting its opening and calcium influx into the cytosol. Because OAADPr is generated directly by sirtuin deacetylase activity, TRPM2 activation acts as a sensor of cellular sirtuin flux and NAD+ utilization. The directionality is unidirectional under basal conditions: sirtuin activity produces OAADPr, which then gates TRPM2, rather than TRPM2 regulating sirtuins. This coupling provides a mechanistic link between metabolic state, redox stress, and calcium-dependent processes such as insulin secretion and apoptotic signaling.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 is the predominant nuclear sirtuin and is enriched at euchromatic regions, where it deacetylates both histones and many transcriptional regulators to shape gene expression. Its nuclear residence allows it to directly access chromatin and nuclear factors such as p53, FOXO, NF-κB, and PGC-1α. Subcellular localization is dynamic and can shift toward DNA double-strand break foci during genotoxic stress, reflecting its role in DNA repair. A caveat is that a fraction of SIRT1 is also cytosolic, so 'nuclear' describes its dominant but not exclusive compartment.

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 is the predominantly cytoplasmic sirtuin and is most abundant in the cytosol, where it deacetylates α-tubulin and a range of metabolic and regulatory proteins. Its localization is cell-cycle regulated, with SIRT2 accumulating and being hyperphosphorylated as cells transit the G2/M boundary. The cytoplasmic residence underpins its roles in microtubule dynamics, mitosis, and cytoplasmic autophagy regulation rather than direct chromatin modification. Note that SIRT2 can also shuttle to the nucleus under certain stress conditions, so localization is not absolute.

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 is the principal mitochondrial sirtuin, imported to the matrix where it removes acetyl, succinyl, and other acyl modifications from respiratory-chain and metabolic enzymes. Its activity is governed by the mitochondrial NAD+/NADH ratio, linking energy state to enzyme function. The directionality is that mitochondrial residence positions SIRT3 to sense and tune local metabolism. Loss of SIRT3 yields oxidative stress and susceptibility to metabolic and cardiac disease.

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 resides in the mitochondrial matrix and acts mainly as a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase on metabolic enzymes such as GDH and MTPα. Its mitochondrial localization enables direct control of amino-acid and fatty-acid fueling of the TCA cycle. The directionality is SIRT4 positioned to brake mitochondrial anabolism. Its activity often opposes the protective actions of SIRT3.

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 localizes to the mitochondrial matrix and is specialized for removing lysine succinyl, malonyl, and glutaryl groups from metabolic enzymes including CPS1, HMGCS2, and β-oxidation/TCA enzymes. Its mitochondrial residence makes it a key regulator of catabolic flux during fasting. The directionality is SIRT5 sensing mitochondrial acylation state to optimize energy production. It is the sole mammalian member of an ancient prokaryotic sirtuin class.

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 is a nuclear sirtuin enriched at heterochromatic and telomeric regions, where it deacetylates H3K9 and H3K56 and performs mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1. Its heterochromatin association is critical for genome stability, telomere maintenance, and suppression of repetitive elements such as LINE-1. SIRT6 thus integrates chromatin regulation with metabolic control of glycolysis, DNA repair, and inflammation. Loss of SIRT6 produces a pronounced premature-aging phenotype, highlighting its non-redundant role in the nucleus.

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 is concentrated in the nucleolus, the site of ribosomal DNA transcription and ribosome biogenesis, where it deacetylates histone H3K18 and regulates RNA polymerase I. Its nucleolar residence positions it to control rRNA synthesis and, consequently, protein synthetic capacity and growth. SIRT7 also deacetylates extra-nucleolar targets such as GATA4 and SMAD3, linking it to cardiac and fibrotic pathways. Deficiency of SIRT7 yields extensive myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy, revealing its importance in stress responses of the heart.

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 functions principally as a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase, using NAD+ to attach a single ADP-ribose group to target lysines rather than removing acetyl marks. Its best-characterized ADP-ribosylation target is glutamate dehydrogenase, whose activity it inhibits to dampen amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion. This enzymatic orientation means SIRT4 generally acts as a metabolic suppressor within mitochondria, opposing anabolic and growth signals. A caveat is that SIRT4's deacetylase activity is weak in vitro, so ADP-ribosylation is its physiologically dominant modality.

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 possesses both deacetylase and mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activities, the latter being particularly important for its chromatin functions. Through ADP-ribosylation of KAP1, SIRT6 recruits HP1α to LINE-1 loci, promoting heterochromatinization and silencing of retrotransposons. The directionality is that SIRT6 is the enzyme and KAP1 (and downstream HP1α) the recipients of the ADP-ribose modification. This activity is independent of its deacetylase function and is selectively enhanced by certain natural activators such as fucoidan.

subject: Caloric Restriction
context: In yeast, the replicative lifespan extension conferred by caloric restriction is abolished when the SIR2 gene is deleted, establishing Sir2 as a required mediator of the CR response. This dependence reflects the fact that CR raises the NAD+/nicotinamide ratio, which relieves nicotinamide feedback inhibition and boosts Sir2 deacetylase activity. The relationship is directional: CR acts upstream and Sir2 is the necessary downstream effector in this genetic pathway. A caveat is that in higher organisms the requirement is distributed across multiple sirtuins and redundant pathways, so SIR2/SIRT1 is necessary but not solely sufficient.

subject: Caloric Restriction
context: Reducing glucose from 2% to 0.5% in yeast medium extends replicative lifespan by roughly 30%, an effect mediated through elevated NAD+ availability and Sir2 activation. The mechanism hinges on CR lowering the nicotinamide/NAD+ ratio, thereby disinhibiting Sir2 and reinforcing silencing at repetitive rDNA and subtelomeric regions. This intervention is directional: the dietary manipulation is the cause and the lifespan gain the consequence. The finding seeded the broader hypothesis that sirtuin activation underlies longevity benefits of restricted feeding across species.

subject: Caloric Restriction
context: Dietary restriction in Drosophila extends lifespan and, as in yeast, this benefit requires the dSir2 (Sir2) gene, indicating evolutionary conservation of the sirtuin-mediated CR pathway. The effect is thought to operate through improved protein homeostasis, stress resistance, and metabolic efficiency rather than simple calorie shortage. Directionally, reduced nutrient signaling upstream engages dSir2 to produce the longevity phenotype. Caveats include that the magnitude and requirement vary with sex, genetic background, and the precise restriction paradigm used.

subject: Caloric Restriction
context: In rodents, caloric restriction raises SIRT1 levels in multiple tissues, and this elevation is linked to reduced inflammatory and oxidative responses. Higher SIRT1 expression translates into enhanced deacetylation of targets such as NF-κB, FOXO, and PGC-1α, promoting stress resistance and metabolic health. The directionality is that CR is the upstream stimulus and increased SIRT1 abundance/activity the downstream mediator. This adaptation is considered a key explanation for the anti-aging and disease-protective effects of CR in mammals.

subject: Caloric Restriction
context: Caloric restriction elevates the brain NAD+/nicotinamide ratio, which both supplies more co-substrate for sirtuins and relieves nicotinamide-mediated feedback inhibition of SIRT1. The resulting gain in sirtuin activity supports neuronal stress resistance, mitochondrial function, and suppression of neuroinflammatory signaling. The relationship is directional: CR shifts the ratio upward, which then potentiates sirtuin-dependent protective programs. This mechanism is frequently invoked to explain CR's protective effects against age-related cognitive decline and neurodegenerative pathology.

subject: Caloric Restriction
context: In pancreatic islets of calorically restricted mice, SIRT4 expression is reduced, shifting the mitochondrial sirtuin balance toward the protective, oxidative-phosphorylation-promoting actions of SIRT3. Because SIRT4 normally restrains amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion and mitochondrial fat oxidation, its downregulation supports improved β-cell metabolic flexibility. The directionality is that CR suppresses SIRT4 transcription, altering the SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio. Aging shows the opposite pattern—rising SIRT4 and falling SIRT3—so CR counters the age-related drift in this ratio.

subject: SIR2 overexpression (yeast)
context: Integration of an extra SIR2 copy in yeast increases replicative lifespan by up to about 30%, implicating Sir2 dosage directly in longevity. The mechanism involves reinforced silencing at rDNA repeats, which reduces spurious recombination and the accumulation of extrachromosomal rDNA circles that drive aging. This is a gain-of-function, directional relationship: more Sir2 yields longer lifespan, though the effect saturates and very high doses can be detrimental. The finding established the foundational idea that boosting sirtuin activity can extend lifespan in a simple eukaryote.

subject: sir-2.1 overexpression (C. elegans)
context: A chromosomal duplication that increases sir-2.1 dosage in C. elegans extends lifespan by up to approximately 50%, paralleling the yeast finding in a multicellular organism. The longevity effect depends on intact insulin/IGF-1-like signaling, because sir-2.1 acts downstream of the DAF-2 pathway to promote stress resistance. The relationship is directional: elevated sir-2.1 produces the lifespan gain. A key caveat is that the requirement for DAF-16 (FOXO) ties sirtuin longevity to the conserved FOXO transcription-factor network.

subject: sir-2.1 lifespan extension
context: The lifespan extension produced by sir-2.1 overexpression in C. elegans is strictly dependent on the forkhead transcription factor DAF-16, the worm FOXO ortholog. DAF-16 is the downstream effector that induces stress-resistance and xenobiotic-detoxification genes once sir-2.1 releases it from repression. Mechanistically, sir-2.1 deacetylates and cooperates with DAF-16 to drive the longevity transcriptional program. Thus the directionality is sir-2.1 → DAF-16 → lifespan, and removing DAF-16 abolishes the benefit.

subject: dSir2 overexpression (Drosophila)
context: Ubiquitous overexpression of the Drosophila Sir2 ortholog extends female lifespan by about 29%, with a more modest or absent effect in males. The sexually dimorphic response reflects differences in nutrient sensing and reproductive physiology between the sexes. Directionally, increased dSir2 acts upstream to produce the longevity phenotype, consistent with the conserved sirtuin-CR axis. As in worms, the effect is intertwined with insulin/FOXO signaling and dietary restriction pathways.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates p53 at multiple lysine residues, dampening p53's transcriptional activation of pro-apoptotic and senescence genes and promoting cell survival under stress. The modification reduces p53's DNA-binding and coactivator recruitment at target promoters. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatically inhibiting p53's tumor-suppressive output. This dual role—protective in normal tissue yet potentially oncogenic—is a defining feature of SIRT1 biology.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 removes acetyl groups from Lys9 and Lys26 of linker histone H1, a modification that influences higher-order chromatin compaction and gene accessibility. Deacetylated H1 is generally associated with a more condensed, transcriptionally repressed chromatin state at SIRT1-target loci. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts enzymatically on H1 to remodel chromatin and silence specific programs. Because H1 links nucleosomes, this action helps SIRT1 enforce long-range repression independently of core histone modifications.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates Lys14 of histone H3, a mark associated with active transcription, thereby contributing to gene silencing at targeted promoters. Loss of H3K14ac reduces promoter accessibility and cooperates with other repressive modifications to restrain transcription. The directionality is strictly enzymatic: SIRT1 removes the acetyl mark, shifting chromatin toward repression. This activity underlies many of SIRT1's roles in repressing inflammatory and metabolic gene programs.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 removes the acetyl group from Lys16 of histone H4, a site whose acetylation is linked to telomeric and rDNA silencing and genome stability. Deacetylation at H4K16 promotes a more compact chromatin fiber and is shared with SIRT2 at this residue in certain contexts. The relationship is directional and repressive: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation consolidates heterochromatin-like states. Defective H4K16 deacetylation is associated with the genomic instability seen when SIRT1 function is compromised.

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of p53
context: By deacetylating p53, SIRT1 lowers p53's transcriptional activation of BH3-only proteins and other apoptotic effectors, suppressing programmed cell death after oxidative or genotoxic stress. This creates a survival bias that helps cells tolerate damage but can also protect incipient cancer cells from elimination. The directionality is that SIRT1 activity on p53 is upstream of reduced apoptosis. A caveat is that chronic suppression of p53-dependent apoptosis is a double-edged sword: protective in normal tissue but potentially tumor-promoting.

subject: HIC1
context: HIC1 (hypermethylated in cancer 1) is a tumor suppressor that binds the SIRT1 promoter via its POZ domain and directly represses SIRT1 transcription. Because p53 transactivates HIC1, a negative feedback loop exists: p53 induces HIC1, which then restrains SIRT1, preventing excessive p53 deacetylation and preserving p53 tumor-suppressive capacity. The directionality is HIC1 → SIRT1 repression, upstream of SIRT1's inhibition of p53. Disruption of this loop in cancer can unleash SIRT1 to silence p53.

subject: p53
context: p53 directly activates transcription of HIC1, a tumor suppressor that in turn represses the SIRT1 promoter, forming a negative feedback loop on SIRT1. This loop ensures that p53 activity is not indefinitely suppressed by SIRT1-mediated deacetylation. Directionally, p53 is the transcription factor and HIC1 the induced target gene. The biological significance is genome protection: by inducing HIC1, p53 prevents SIRT1 from over-deacetylating and silencing p53 itself.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates Ku70, the DNA-repair factor and regulatory subunit of the Ku complex that also binds and inhibits the pro-apoptotic protein Bax. Deacetylation of Ku70 increases its affinity for Bax, sequestering Bax away from mitochondria. The directionality is enzymatic: SIRT1 removes acetyl marks from Ku70 to modulate its protein-interaction state. This mechanism couples SIRT1's DNA-repair functions to a direct anti-apoptotic, cell-survival program.

subject: Deacetylated Ku70
context: Once deacetylated by SIRT1, Ku70 binds the BH3 domain of the pro-apoptotic protein Bax and retains it in the cytosol, preventing Bax translocation to and permeabilization of mitochondria. This sequestration blocks the intrinsic apoptosis cascade downstream of many stress signals. The relationship is directional: deacetylated Ku70 is the binding partner that neutralizes Bax. The net effect is cytoprotection, though as with p53 suppression this can also shield damaged cells in oncogenic contexts.

subject: E2F1
context: The E2F1 transcription factor binds directly to the SIRT1 promoter and activates its transcription, particularly under proliferative or DNA-damage signals. This positions SIRT1 as a downstream effector of E2F1-driven programs that balance cell-cycle progression with survival. The directionality is E2F1 → SIRT1 gene activation. Notably, the relationship is reciprocal, because SIRT1 then feeds back to inhibit E2F1's apoptotic function.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 interacts with and deacetylates E2F1, converting it from a potent inducer of apoptosis into a less active transcriptional partner and thereby blocking E2F1-dependent cell death. This creates a feedback loop in which E2F1 induces SIRT1, and SIRT1 then restrains E2F1's apoptotic output. The directionality is SIRT1 acting upstream to suppress E2F1's deadly transcriptional program. The net consequence is enhanced cell survival under stress, with implications for both tissue homeostasis and tumorigenesis.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates the forkhead factor FOXO1, redirecting its transcriptional program toward metabolic homeostasis and stress resistance while tempering apoptosis. Deacetylated FOXO1 cooperates with C/EBPα to induce adiponectin and with PGC-1α to support oxidative metabolism. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic modification of FOXO1. This regulation is central to SIRT1 control of glucose handling and insulin sensitivity.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a in multiple cell types, including neurons and fibroblasts, shifting its target-gene program toward stress resistance and away from apoptosis. Deacetylated FOXO3a induces antioxidant enzymes such as SOD2 and catalase and promotes autophagy while reducing death-gene expression. The directionality is SIRT1 → FOXO3a modification → altered transcription. This axis is a major mechanism by which SIRT1 confers longevity- and stress-resistance phenotypes.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO4, which reverts FOXO4-mediated suppression and enhances cellular defenses against oxidative stress. Deacetylation of FOXO4 boosts expression of DNA-repair and antioxidant genes such as GADD45 while suppressing caspase activation. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 enzymatically licenses FOXO4 to drive protective transcription. This contributes to SIRT1's broad role in genomic maintenance and resilience to damage.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates the RelA/p65 subunit of NF-κB, particularly at Lys310, reducing its ability to recruit the transcriptional machinery and activate pro-inflammatory genes. This post-translational modification dampens NF-κB target genes such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. The directionality is SIRT1 acting enzymatically on RelA to inhibit inflammatory transcription. Because NF-κB drives chronic inflammation implicated in aging and disease, SIRT1's action is a key anti-inflammatory node.

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of RelA/p65
context: Deacetylation of RelA/p65 by SIRT1 lowers NF-κB transactivation, thereby reducing expression of cytokines, chemokines, and adhesion molecules that propagate inflammation. This directly opposes the pro-inflammatory program and underlies many of SIRT1's protective effects in metabolic, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative contexts. The directionality is SIRT1 deacetylation → suppressed NF-κB signaling. A caveat is that excessive NF-κB suppression could impair host defense, so the effect is beneficial within physiological ranges.

subject: Cigarette smoke
context: Exposure to cigarette-smoke extract disrupts the SIRT1–RelA/p65 complex, diminishing deacetylation of RelA and leaving NF-κB in a more active, pro-inflammatory state. The consequence is heightened expression of inflammatory mediators in airway and other cells exposed to smoke. The directionality is that the environmental insult (smoke) reduces a protective protein–protein interaction, increasing inflammation. This provides a mechanistic link between smoking, impaired sirtuin function, and chronic inflammatory lung disease.

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 expression is significantly elevated in breast carcinoma compared with normal breast tissue, and high SIRT7 correlates with poorer prognosis in several tumor types. Its overexpression supports tumor growth and ribosomal biogenesis, and it can deacetylate oncogenic transcription factors such as GATA4. The directionality is that increased SIRT7 abundance is associated with and likely promotes malignant phenotypes. A caveat is that sirtuin roles in cancer are context-dependent, and SIRT7 can be either tumor-promoting or, in some tissues, tumor-suppressive.

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 activates RNA polymerase I-mediated transcription of ribosomal DNA, driving ribosome biogenesis and protein synthetic capacity in proliferating cells. It does so in part through deacetylation of histone H3K18 at rDNA and by stabilizing the Pol I transcriptional apparatus. The directionality is SIRT7 → enhanced rRNA production → increased ribosome output. Because uncontrolled ribosome biogenesis fuels tumor growth, this activity aligns with SIRT7's oncogenic associations.

subject: SIRT1
object: RNA Polymerase I transcription (via TAFI68 deacetylation)
context: SIRT1 deacetylates TAFI68, a subunit of the RNA polymerase I transcription factor complex, decreasing its DNA-binding activity and thereby repressing rRNA transcription. This contrasts with SIRT7, which activates Pol I, illustrating divergent sirtuin control of ribosome biogenesis. The directionality is SIRT1 → TAFI68 deacetylation → Pol I repression. By limiting ribosome production, SIRT1 can restrain growth and oppose the biosynthetic programs favored in cancer and hypertrophy.

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 resides in a genomic region frequently deleted in human gliomas, and re-expression of SIRT2 markedly reduces colony formation by glioma cells, indicating tumor-suppressor function. Its activity deacetylates substrates such as α-tubulin and HNF4α that govern mitotic fidelity and metabolism. The directionality is that SIRT2 loss permits, and SIRT2 restoration suppresses, gliomagenesis. A caveat is that SIRT2 can act as either tumor suppressor or promoter depending on tissue and context.

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 deacetylates Lys16 on histone H4, a modification linked to chromatin condensation during the G2/M transition of mitosis. Removing H4K16ac promotes a more compact mitotic chromatin state compatible with chromosome segregation. The directionality is enzymatic: SIRT2 directly deacetylates H4K16 to remodel chromatin at division. This activity complements SIRT2's role in microtubule and cell-cycle regulation.

subject: SIRT2 expression
context: SIRT2 protein levels rise dramatically as cells enter mitosis and the enzyme is hyperphosphorylated at the G2/M boundary, timing its activity to chromosome condensation and division. This cell-cycle coupling links SIRT2 to proper mitotic progression and genomic stability. The directionality is that the G2/M transition drives SIRT2 upregulation and activation. Loss or dysregulation of this peak is associated with mitotic defects and, in some cancers, genomic instability.

subject: SIRT6 knockout mice
context: Mice lacking SIRT6 develop a striking premature-aging syndrome with reduced size, loss of subcutaneous fat, lymphopenia, colitis, and spinal curvature, dying early. The phenotype reflects defective base-excision repair, genomic instability, and metabolic and inflammatory dysregulation. The directionality is SIRT6 deficiency → multisystem premature aging. This makes SIRT6 one of the clearest single-gene links between sirtuins and mammalian longevity.

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 is required for efficient base-excision repair (BER), the pathway that removes oxidized and alkylated bases, and SIRT6-deficient cells accumulate DNA damage from defective BER. SIRT6 supports BER in part by mono-ADP-ribosylating and recruiting repair factors and by maintaining heterochromatin at damaged sites. The directionality is SIRT6 activity upstream of proper BER execution. This function explains the genomic instability and premature aging of SIRT6 knockout mice.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates Lys50 of the HIV-1 transactivator Tat, a modification that increases Tat's affinity for the viral LTR and its ability to recruit the transcription machinery. This enzymatic action therefore activates, rather than suppresses, the viral protein. The directionality is SIRT1 → Tat activation → enhanced viral transcription. This reveals an unexpected pro-viral role for the otherwise cytoprotective SIRT1.

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of Tat
context: Because deacetylated Tat is a more potent transactivator, SIRT1-mediated deacetylation at Lys50 boosts HIV-1 transcription from the proviral LTR. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Tat to amplify viral gene expression. This positions host SIRT1 as a cofactor that HIV exploits, a caveat to the generally beneficial reputation of SIRT1 activation. Targeting this interaction is of interest for antiviral strategies.

subject: SIRT1
context: In white adipose tissue, SIRT1 promotes lipolysis and fat mobilization by repressing adipogenic transcription factors such as PPAR-γ and aP2 and by co-ordinating catabolic gene programs. This shifts storage tissue from lipid accumulation toward fatty-acid release for oxidation. The directionality is SIRT1 → repression of adipogenesis → enhanced fat mobilization. These actions contribute to the lean phenotype and metabolic health seen under caloric restriction.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 represses PPAR-γ, the master regulator of adipogenesis, by deacetylating and interfering with its co-activator interactions, thereby inhibiting differentiation of preadipocytes into fat cells. Pharmacological SIRT1 activation or overexpression recapitulates this repression and blocks adipogenesis. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of PPAR-γ suppression. This mechanism underlies SIRT1's anti-obesity and insulin-sensitizing effects.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates the peroxisome-proliferator-activated-receptor-γ coactivator 1α (PGC-1α), switching it from a repressed to an active transcriptional coactivator that drives mitochondrial and oxidative-metabolism genes. Deacetylated PGC-1α migrates to the nucleus and induces oxidative phosphorylation and gluconeogenic programs. The directionality is SIRT1 → PGC-1α activation → metabolic remodeling. This axis is central to SIRT1's roles in energy homeostasis, exercise response, and CR benefits.

subject: PGC-1α
context: PGC-1α is the master coactivator controlling mitochondrial biogenesis, stimulating transcription of nuclear-encoded respiratory-chain subunits and coordinating with mitochondrial DNA replication. Its activation by SIRT1 (and AMPK) increases mitochondrial number and oxidative capacity. The directionality is PGC-1α upstream of new mitochondrion formation. This program underlies improved endurance, metabolic flexibility, and resistance to oxidative stress.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 transcriptionally represses UCP2, a mitochondrial inner-membrane uncoupler that dissipates the proton gradient and reduces ATP yield. In SIRT1 knockout mice, UCP2 is upregulated, lowering ATP production in pancreatic β-cells. The directionality is SIRT1 → suppression of UCP2 expression. By keeping UCP2 low, SIRT1 preserves the mitochondrial membrane potential needed for efficient ATP generation and insulin secretion.

subject: SIRT1 repression of UCP2
context: Repression of UCP2 by SIRT1 preserves mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis in pancreatic β-cells, which raises the ATP/ADP ratio and closes KATP channels to trigger insulin release. Mice overexpressing SIRT1 in β-cells show enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. The directionality is SIRT1 → UCP2 downregulation → stronger insulin secretion. This links SIRT1 to improved glucose homeostasis and protection against diabetes.

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 deacetylates and activates acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (AceCS2) in the mitochondrial matrix, enabling it to convert acetate into acetyl-CoA for the TCA cycle and lipogenesis. Deacetylation relieves autoinhibition, increasing AceCS2 catalytic efficiency. The directionality is SIRT3 → AceCS2 activation → acetyl-CoA production. This allows mitochondria to use acetate as an alternative carbon source, contributing to metabolic flexibility during fasting.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates and activates acetyl-CoA synthetase 1 (AceCS1) in the cytoplasm, analogous to SIRT3's activation of the mitochondrial AceCS2, permitting acetate utilization outside the mitochondrion. Activated AceCS1 supplies cytosolic acetyl-CoA for chromatin and lipid metabolism. The directionality is SIRT1 → AceCS1 activation. Together with SIRT3, this shows sirtuins broadly license acetate salvage across compartments.

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 lowers mitochondrial ROS by deacetylating and activating antioxidant enzymes such as MnSOD and components of the electron-transport chain, while also reducing mitochondrial membrane potential in a manner that limits superoxide leak. Higher SIRT3 activity therefore shifts the mitochondrial redox balance toward less oxidative damage. The directionality is SIRT3 activity upstream of reduced ROS. This antioxidant function is a major basis for SIRT3's protective roles in heart, liver, and aging.

subject: SIRT3
context: Cold exposure induces SIRT3 in brown adipose tissue, where it promotes expression of mitochondrial genes and supports thermogenic programs. The induction enhances oxidative metabolism and uncoupled respiration needed for heat production. The directionality is cold stimulus → SIRT3 upregulation → thermogenic mitochondrial biogenesis. This ties SIRT3 to adaptive thermogenesis and the metabolic benefits of cold exposure.

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 mono-ADP-ribosylates glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH), inhibiting its oxidative deamination of glutamate to α-ketoglutarate and thereby slowing anaplerotic carbon entry into the TCA cycle. This restrains amino-acid-derived ATP production and insulin secretion in β-cells. The directionality is SIRT4 enzymatic inhibition of GDH. SIRT4 thus acts as a mitochondrial brake on amino-acid catabolism, opposing anabolic fueling of secretion.

subject: SIRT4 inhibition of GDH
context: By inhibiting GDH, SIRT4 blunts the ability of amino acids such as leucine to stimulate insulin release from pancreatic β-cells, because less α-ketoglutarate is generated to elevate ATP and trigger secretion. The relationship is directional: SIRT4-mediated GDH inhibition → reduced amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion. This positions SIRT4 as a physiological negative regulator of nutrient-particular insulin release.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 protects neurons from β-amyloid-induced toxicity, in part by inhibiting NF-κB signaling in microglia and reducing neuroinflammation, and by supporting neuronal stress-resistance pathways. This limits the inflammatory and oxidative damage that accompany amyloid pathology. The directionality is SIRT1 activity upstream of reduced neuronal injury. The effect dovetails with observations that caloric restriction, which raises SIRT1, protects against Alzheimer's-like neuropathology.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 confers neuroprotection partly through deacetylation and activation of PGC-1α, which drives mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant defenses in neurons. Enhanced PGC-1α activity counters the energetic and oxidative deficits underlying neurodegeneration. The directionality is SIRT1 → PGC-1α → neuronal resilience. This axis is a leading explanation for how SIRT1 activation benefits Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and other neurodegenerative models.

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol, a plant polyphenol produced under stress, was the first widely studied small-molecule activator of mammalian SIRT1, identified in a screen for compounds that extend yeast lifespan via Sir2. It binds the SIRT1 N-terminal domain near Glu230, lowering the enzyme's Km for peptide and NAD+ substrates and boosting deacetylation. The directionality is resveratrol upstream as an allosteric activator of SIRT1. A caveat is that its in vivo relevance is debated because systemic concentrations achieved after oral dosing are low.

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol extends lifespan in yeast through a Sir2-dependent mechanism, mirroring the effect of caloric restriction and establishing it as a prototypical sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). The lifespan gain requires SIR2, confirming that the compound works through the sirtuin axis rather than an independent pathway. The directionality is resveratrol → Sir2 activation → longevity. These findings launched the modern field of sirtuin-targeted longevity therapeutics.

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol's lifespan-extending effect in yeast is absolutely dependent on the presence of the SIR2 gene, so SIR2 deletion abolishes the benefit. This genetic requirement demonstrated that resveratrol acts through sirtuin activation rather than off-target longevity pathways. The directionality is resveratrol upstream, SIR2 downstream and necessary. The dependence established the conceptual template later applied to mammalian SIRT1 STACs.

subject: Resveratrol (high-calorie diet mice)
context: In mice on a high-calorie diet, resveratrol increases mitochondrial number and function, an effect accompanied by elevated SIRT1 and PGC-1α activity. This shift counters diet-induced metabolic dysfunction by improving oxidative capacity. The directionality is resveratrol upstream, activating SIRT1/PGC-1α to drive mitochondrial biogenesis. The finding helped popularize resveratrol as a CR-mimetic against diet-induced obesity.

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol treatment lowers blood glucose and circulating insulin in animals on a high-calorie diet, improving glycemic control. These metabolic benefits are linked to SIRT1/AMPK activation and improved insulin sensitivity in liver and muscle. The directionality is resveratrol → SIRT1/AMPK → reduced glycemia. Caveats include that human trials have been inconsistent, likely owing to poor bioavailability.

subject: SIRT3 gene variant (intron 5 enhancer)
context: A polymorphism in an intron-5 enhancer of the SIRT3 gene is associated with exceptional longevity (age beyond 90 years) specifically in men. The variant is thought to alter SIRT3 expression or regulation, conferring enhanced mitochondrial stress resistance. The directionality is genetic variation associated with, and putatively causal of, prolonged lifespan. As a correlation, it supports but does not prove that higher SIRT3 activity promotes human longevity.

subject: SIRT1 allele variants
context: Several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the human SIRT1 gene are significantly associated with systemic energy expenditure in Finnish cohorts, suggesting that SIRT1 variation influences metabolic rate. These variants may alter SIRT1 expression or activity, shifting how individuals burn fuel. The directionality is genetic SIRT1 variation linked to energy-expenditure phenotype. As with most GWAS associations, effect sizes are modest and context-dependent.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 binds the androgen receptor and deacetylates it at Lys630 within the lysine motif, repressing AR transcriptional activity and its oncogenic signaling in prostate tissue. This enzymatic modification dampens AR-driven proliferative programs. The directionality is SIRT1 acting upstream to inhibit AR. This axis is relevant to prostate cancer, where SIRT1 can oppose androgen-dependent tumor growth.

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 interacts with HOXA10, a conserved homeobox transcription factor critical for embryonic cell-type determination and adult tissue homeostasis. The interaction suggests SIRT2 influences HOXA10-dependent transcriptional programs, though the precise deacetylation outcome is less characterized. The directionality is SIRT2 engaging HOXA10 as a partner/substrate. This connection links SIRT2 to developmental regulation and possibly to differentiation defects in disease.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 physically interacts with the bHLH transcriptional repressors Hes1 and Hey2 both in vitro and in vivo, modulating their ability to repress target promoters. Deacetylation by SIRT1 can alter the DNA-binding or co-repressor recruitment of these factors. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatically tuning Hes1/Hey2 repression. This intersects with Notch and VEGF signaling and with SIRT1's neuroprotective regulation of BDNF.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1-null mice are markedly smaller, grow slowly, and show defects in eye morphogenesis and cardiac septation, revealing SIRT1's role in normal development. These phenotypes indicate that SIRT1 is not merely a stress-response protein but is required for organogenesis. The directionality is SIRT1 deficiency causing structural developmental abnormalities. The perinatal lethality of many knockouts limited study, prompting tissue-specific models.

subject: SIRT1
context: Surviving SIRT1 knockout mice of both sexes are sterile: males have low sperm counts and females fail to ovulate, implicating SIRT1 in gametogenesis and reproductive endocrine control. The defect reflects failed differentiation and stress responses in gonadal tissues. The directionality is SIRT1 loss upstream of reproductive failure. This shows SIRT1 is essential for germ-cell development and fertility.

subject: Nmnat (NAD+ biosynthetic enzyme)
context: Nmnat, the NAD+-biosynthetic enzyme, protects axons from Wallerian degeneration largely by raising NAD+ and thereby activating SIRT1, which supports axonal survival after injury. The protection is upstream of SIRT1-dependent maintenance of mitochondrial and chromatin function in neurons. The directionality is Nmnat → NAD+ → SIRT1 → axonal protection. This established a key NAD+/sirtuin axis in neuronal resilience.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates Smad7 at Lys60 and Lys70, which enhances Smad7's recognition by the E3 ligase Smurf1 and targets it for ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation. This accelerates turnover of the TGF-β inhibitory Smad, modulating TGF-β pathway intensity. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic marking of Smad7 for destruction. The consequence is context-dependent regulation of TGF-β signaling rather than simple inhibition.

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of Smad7
context: By promoting degradation of Smad7, SIRT1 deacetylation tempers TGF-β signaling in glomerular mesangial cells and protects them from TGF-β-dependent apoptosis. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Smad7 to relieve a pro-apoptotic TGF-β output. This renoprotective mechanism is relevant to diabetic nephropathy and other glomerulopathies. It illustrates how sirtuin control of a single substrate can determine cell fate in injury.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates Lys115 and Lys121 of the histone variant H2A.Z, a mark that licenses H2A.Z for ubiquitination and proteasome-dependent degradation. Removing these acetyl groups thus destabilizes H2A.Z at chromatin. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic modification upstream of H2A.Z clearance. Because H2A.Z promotes pathological hypertrophy, its removal is protective in the heart.

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of H2A.Z
context: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation and degradation of H2A.Z helps protect the heart from failure by removing a histone variant that drives maladaptive cardiac hypertrophic gene programs. The directionality is SIRT1 → H2A.Z loss → attenuated hypertrophy. This is a mechanistically plausible explanation for why SIRT1 activation is cardioprotective, though the in vivo evidence carries moderate confidence (0.75). It links chromatin dynamics directly to heart disease resistance.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 negatively regulates the histone acetyltransferase p300 by deacetylating it at Lys1020 and Lys1024, reducing p300's enzymatic and coactivator activity. This counterbalances p300-driven acetylation of chromatin and transcription factors. The directionality is SIRT1 inhibiting a major acetyltransferase, creating a rheostat between acetylation and deacetylation. This crosstalk helps SIRT1 enforce repression of inflammatory and growth genes.

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 is expressed in oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells, the myelin-forming glia of CNS and PNS respectively, where it deacetylates α-tubulin and regulates microtubule stability. Its presence in myelinating cells ties SIRT2 to axonal support and myelin integrity. The directionality is SIRT2 acting within glia to control cytoskeletal dynamics. Dysregulation is implicated in demyelinating and neurodegenerative conditions.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 inhibits myogenesis by deacetylating histones H3K9 and H3K14 at the promoters of myogenin and myosin heavy chain, repressing muscle-gene expression. This keeps myoblasts in a less differentiated state under certain conditions. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of suppressed muscle differentiation. However, SIRT1 can also support muscle maintenance under stress, so context matters.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 activators promote osteoblast differentiation while suppressing adipocyte formation from mesenchymal progenitors, biasing lineage commitment toward bone. This effect is linked to SIRT1's repression of PPAR-γ and support of RUNX2/osteogenic programs. The directionality is SIRT1 favoring osteogenesis over adipogenesis. The association carries moderate confidence (0.75) but has therapeutic implications for osteoporosis. Importantly, it complements SIRT1's opposing action on myogenesis, underscoring context dependence.

subject: p33ING1b
context: In hepatocarcinoma, p33ING1b binds SIRT1 and blocks its ability to deacetylate p53, thereby preserving p53's transcriptional activity, including repression of α-fetoprotein (AFP). This relieves SIRT1-mediated inhibition of p53 tumor suppression. The directionality is p33ING1b antagonizing SIRT1 at the p53 node. The interaction reveals a tissue-specific brake on SIRT1's pro-survival, potentially oncogenic, action.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO1 and enhances its interaction with C/EBPα, a combination that drives transcription of the adiponectin gene and raises circulating adiponectin. Adiponectin in turn improves insulin sensitivity and has anti-inflammatory effects. The directionality is SIRT1 → FOXO1/C/EBPα → adiponectin expression. This links SIRT1 to beneficial adipokine secretion and metabolic health.

subject: Adiponectin
context: Administration of adiponectin to obese, high-fat-fed mice improves insulin sensitivity and lowers blood glucose, reflecting its role as a insulin-sensitizing adipokine. It acts through AdipoR1/2 receptors to activate AMPK and PPAR-α pathways that enhance fatty-acid oxidation. The directionality is adiponectin upstream of improved insulin action. Because SIRT1 raises adiponectin, this forms part of SIRT1's anti-diabetic circuitry.

subject: Caloric Restriction
context: In mouse models engineered to develop Alzheimer's-like pathology, caloric restriction prevents accumulation of β-amyloid neuropathology, an effect consistent with SIRT1-driven reductions in neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. The directionality is CR upstream of reduced amyloid burden. This supports the hypothesis that CR protects the brain through sirtuin-mediated resilience. Human translation remains uncertain but motivates lifestyle interventions in neurodegeneration.

subject: PGC-1α knockout mice
object: MPTP and kainic acid neuronal damage
context: Mice lacking PGC-1α are markedly more sensitive to neuronal loss induced by MPTP (a dopaminergic toxin) and kainic acid (an excitotoxin), revealing PGC-1α's role in neuronal stress resistance. Because SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, this sensitivity indirectly implicates the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis in neuroprotection. The directionality is PGC-1α deficiency → heightened vulnerability. The phenotype mirrors features of Parkinson's and other neurodegenerative models.

subject: Sirtuins
context: The sirtuin family comprises seven mammalian members (SIRT1–SIRT7) plus the ancestral yeast Sir2, all sharing an NAD+-dependent catalytic core that performs deacetylation and ADP-ribosylation. They differ in subcellular localization—nuclear (SIRT1, SIRT6, SIRT7), cytoplasmic (SIRT2), and mitochondrial (SIRT3, SIRT4, SIRT5)—which dictates their substrate portfolios. The directionality is that NAD+ is the obligate co-substrate for every family member. This unifying dependence ties sirtuin activity to the cellular energy and redox state.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates and activates PGC-1α, converting it into a potent coactivator of mitochondrial and oxidative-metabolism genes. Deacetylated PGC-1α enters the nucleus to drive oxidative phosphorylation and gluconeogenesis. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of PGC-1α activation. This is a canonical node linking sirtuins to energy expenditure and longevity.

subject: SIRT1
context: Through deacetylation and activation of PGC-1α (and cooperation with AMPK), SIRT1 promotes the transcription of nuclear- and mitochondrial-encoded respiratory-chain components, increasing mitochondrial number and function. The directionality is SIRT1/PGC-1α upstream of new mitochondrion formation. This program underlies many metabolic and neuroprotective benefits attributed to SIRT1 activation and to caloric restriction.

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 inhibits glutamate dehydrogenase by mono-ADP-ribosylation, reducing conversion of glutamate to α-ketoglutarate and limiting anaplerotic carbon entry into the TCA cycle. The directionality is SIRT4 enzymatic suppression of GDH. This restrains amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion and mitochondrial ATP generation. It marks SIRT4 as a metabolic brake within mitochondria.

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 represses hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) and downstream glycolytic and lipogenic programs, opposing the Warburg-like shift seen in cancer and aging. By limiting HIF-1α target transcription, SIRT6 favors oxidative metabolism and genomic stability. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of HIF-1α suppression. This underlies SIRT6's tumor-suppressive and metabolic-homeostasis roles.

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 regulates rRNA transcription by activating RNA polymerase I and deacetylating histone H3K18 at ribosomal DNA, controlling ribosome biogenesis and protein synthetic capacity. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of Pol I activity and ribosome production. Because excessive ribosome biogenesis fuels proliferation, this activity aligns SIRT7 with growth and, in cancer, with tumor promotion. It also ties SIRT7 to nucleolar stress responses.

subject: CD38
context: Inhibiting CD38, a major consumer of NAD+ that generates nicotinamide and cADPR, preserves cellular NAD+ pools by reducing their catabolic drain. The directionality is CD38 inhibition upstream of higher NAD+ availability. Because all sirtuins require NAD+ as co-substrate, preserving NAD+ indirectly sustains sirtuin activity. This is a leading strategy to reverse age-related NAD+ decline.

subject: CD38
context: By preserving NAD+, CD38 inhibition boosts sirtuin activity, especially mitochondrial SIRT3, which depends on adequate NAD+ to deacetylate metabolic and antioxidant enzymes. The directionality is CD38 inhibition → more NAD+ → heightened SIRT3 function. This indirectly enhances mitochondrial ROS defense and metabolic health. Pharmacologic CD38 blockers such as 78c extend lifespan in aged mice via this axis.

subject: Daratumumab
context: Daratumumab (Darzalex, first approved 2015) and isatuximab (Sarclisa, approved 2020/2021) are IgG1 monoclonal antibodies that bind distinct epitopes on CD38, a cell-surface ectoenzyme. By engaging CD38 on malignant plasma cells, daratumumab triggers antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-dependent killing. The directionality is the antibody acting on CD38-expressing cells. Although primarily an anticancer agent, depleting CD38 also reduces NAD+ consumption, indirectly favoring sirtuin activity.

subject: Isatuximab
context: Isatuximab (Sarclisa) is an IgG1 anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody, approved around 2020/2021, that binds a different CD38 epitope than daratumumab. It mediates direct apoptosis and immune effector functions against CD38+ multiple myeloma cells. The directionality is antibody → CD38 engagement → tumor cell death. Like daratumumab, it also lowers CD38 ectoenzyme activity, indirectly preserving NAD+ for sirtuins.

subject: Daratumumab
context: Daratumumab is a frontline anti-CD38 antibody therapy for multiple myeloma, where CD38 is highly expressed on malignant plasma cells. Its clinical efficacy stems from direct and immune-mediated elimination of these cells. The directionality is daratumumab upstream of myeloma cell clearance. Beyond oncology, its CD38 inhibition has the secondary effect of sparing NAD+ pools that sirtuins depend on.

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol binds the N-terminal domain of SIRT1 at Glu230, inducing a conformational change that lowers the enzyme's Km for peptide/NAD+ substrates such as PGC-1α and FOXO3a, thereby allosterically enhancing deacetylation. The directionality is resveratrol acting directly on SIRT1 as a sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). This direct mechanism complements an indirect cAMP/AMPK/NAD+ pathway. A caveat is that the affinity is modest and physiological relevance depends on achievable tissue concentrations.

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol competitively inhibits cAMP phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4), the enzyme that degrades cAMP to AMP, thereby slowing cAMP clearance. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of PDE4 inhibition. This indirect action raises intracellular cAMP, which then engages the Epac1/Ca2+/AMPK/NAMPT cascade that further activates SIRT1. It is one arm of resveratrol's dual (direct plus indirect) SIRT1-activation mechanism.

subject: PDE4 inhibition (resveratrol)
context: Inhibiting PDE4 prevents cAMP degradation, so intracellular cAMP accumulates after resveratrol exposure. The directionality is PDE4 inhibition → elevated cAMP. Elevated cAMP then activates the exchange protein Epac1, propagating a calcium and AMPK signal that ultimately boosts NAD+ and SIRT1. This pathway explains how resveratrol can activate SIRT1 even through non-allosteric means.

subject: cAMP (elevated)
context: High intracellular cAMP activates Epac1 (Exchange Protein directly Activated by cAMP), a guanine-nucleotide-exchange factor that triggers downstream signaling independent of PKA. The directionality is cAMP upstream of Epac1 activation. Epac1 then stimulates calcium release from the ER, linking cAMP to Ca2+-dependent kinases. This step is pivotal in resveratrol's indirect SIRT1-activation cascade.

subject: Epac1 activation
context: Epac1 activation induces calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm, raising cytosolic Ca2+ that serves as a second messenger. The directionality is Epac1 upstream of cytoplasmic Ca2+ elevation. The Ca2+ surge then activates CaMKKβ, bridging cAMP signaling to AMPK. This couples resveratrol's PDE4 inhibition to metabolic kinase activation.

subject: Ca2+ surge (cytoplasmic)
context: The cytoplasmic calcium surge activates calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase β (CaMKKβ), which phosphorylates and activates AMPK, the central cellular energy sensor. The directionality is Ca2+ → CaMKKβ → AMPK phosphorylation. Activated AMPK then induces NAMPT and raises NAD+, closing the loop on SIRT1 activation. This is a key branch point linking calcium flux to metabolic homeostasis.

subject: AMPK (activated)
context: Activated AMPK increases expression of NAMPT, the rate-limiting enzyme of the NAD+ salvage pathway that converts nicotinamide to NMN. The directionality is AMPK upstream of NAMPT induction. More NAMPT elevates intracellular NAD+, the obligate co-substrate for sirtuins. This AMPK→NAMPT→NAD+ axis is a major indirect route by which resveratrol and exercise activate SIRT1.

subject: NAMPT upregulation
context: NAMPT is the rate-limiting enzyme in the NAD+ salvage pathway, so its upregulation raises cellular NAD+ levels and fuels sirtuin activity. The directionality is NAMPT increase → NAD+ increase → enhanced sirtuin function. This is the terminal step of resveratrol's indirect activation cascade. Preserving NAD+ via NAMPT (or CD38 inhibition) is a common theme across sirtuin-activating strategies.

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of FOXO3a
context: Deacetylated FOXO3a transcriptionally upregulates endogenous antioxidant enzymes, prominently mitochondrial SOD2 and catalase, bolstering ROS scavenging. The directionality is SIRT1/FOXO3a upstream of increased antioxidant capacity. This reduces oxidative damage in resveratrol-treated cells and animals. It is a central mechanism for sirtuin-mediated protection against aging and metabolic disease.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: Resveratrol-activated SIRT1 deacetylates the NF-κB subunit RelA/p65, preventing its optimal DNA binding and transcriptional activation. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatically inhibiting NF-κB. This suppresses expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines including TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. The anti-inflammatory action is a major contributor to resveratrol's cardiovascular and metabolic benefits.

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of NF-κB
context: By deacetylating NF-κB, SIRT1 reduces transcription of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, dampening the inflammatory transcriptome. The directionality is SIRT1/NF-κB upstream of lower cytokine output. This is mechanistically important in atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, and metabolic inflammation. Resveratrol leverages this axis to curb chronic low-grade inflammation.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1 (resveratrol-activated)
context: Resveratrol-activated endothelial SIRT1 increases eNOS expression and deacetylates/activates it, enhancing nitric-oxide production and promoting vasodilation. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of eNOS activation. Improved NO bioavailability lowers vascular tone and protects against endothelial dysfunction. This underlies resveratrol's cardiovascular and 'French paradox' associations.

subject: SIRT1 activation (resveratrol)
context: Through the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α pathway, resveratrol reduces hepatic steatosis in diet-induced obesity models by enhancing fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial function while limiting lipogenesis. The directionality is SIRT1 activation upstream of reduced liver fat accumulation. This demonstrates a translational metabolic benefit of sirtuin activation. Human efficacy, however, is limited by resveratrol's poor bioavailability.

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol shows a hormetic, biphasic dose-response: at low-to-moderate doses it acts as a mild stressor that triggers beneficial adaptive responses such as sirtuin activation and antioxidant defense, whereas at very high doses it can produce off-target or pro-oxidant effects. The directionality is dose determining outcome, not simple monotonic benefit. This complicates dosing in therapeutics. It also rationalizes why modest, diet-like exposures may be more effective than pharmacological megadoses.

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism—glucuronidation and sulfation in gut and liver—yielding very low systemic free concentrations after oral intake. The directionality is oral administration → rapid conjugation → poor bioavailability. This undermines many preclinical benefits when translating to humans. Strategies such as the red-wine matrix, nanoparticle delivery, or combining with quercetin/ethanol aim to improve exposure.

subject: Honokiol
context: Honokiol, a biphenolic lignan from Magnolia, physically interacts with SIRT3, increasing its deacetylase activity and upregulating SIRT3 protein expression. The directionality is honokiol upstream of SIRT3 activation. This engagement yields downstream deacetylation of mitochondrial antioxidant and metabolic targets. Honokiol thereby mimics caloric-restriction benefits specifically within mitochondria.

subject: SIRT3
context: Honokiol-activated SIRT3 deacetylates MnSOD at Lys68 and Lys122, markedly increasing its superoxide-scavenging activity in the mitochondrial matrix. The directionality is SIRT3 enzymatic activation of MnSOD. Enhanced MnSOD lowers mitochondrial ROS and protects against oxidative injury. This is a principal mechanism for honokiol's cardiorenal and neuroprotective effects.

subject: SIRT3
context: Honokiol-activated SIRT3 deacetylates OSCP, a subunit of the mitochondrial F1Fo-ATP synthase, optimizing coupling of proton flux to ATP synthesis. The directionality is SIRT3 enzymatic tuning of ATP synthase. Improved coupling boosts cellular energy output while limiting proton-leak-associated ROS. This contributes to honokiol's metabolic and cardioprotective actions.

subject: Honokiol
context: Through SIRT3 activation, honokiol reverses pathological cardiac hypertrophy and protects against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in preclinical models. The directionality is honokiol → SIRT3 → antihypertrophic and antioxidant programs. By activating mitochondrial defenses, it counters the oxidative and energetic deficits of failing myocardium. This positions SIRT3 as a therapeutic node in heart failure.

subject: Honokiol
context: Honokiol suppresses renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis by activating SIRT3, which inhibits the NF-κB/TGF-β1 pathway and limits fibrogenic signaling in kidney tubules. The directionality is honokiol → SIRT3 → antifibrotic transcription. This reduces collagen deposition and inflammatory infiltrate. It illustrates SIRT3's broad tissue-protective role beyond the heart.

subject: Dihydromyricetin
context: Dihydromyricetin (DHM), a flavonoid from vine tea, activates SIRT3 mitochondrial deacetylase activity, leading to MnSOD deacetylation and lowered ROS. The directionality is DHM upstream of SIRT3 activation. This mitochondrial action underlies DHM's hepatoprotective and metabolic benefits. DHM also activates AMPK, synergizing with SIRT3 via NAD+ elevation.

subject: Dihydromyricetin
context: DHM activates AMPK, which synergistically raises NAD+ via NAMPT upregulation and thereby further potentiates SIRT3 activity. The directionality is DHM → AMPK → NAD+ → SIRT3. This dual SIRT3/AMPK engagement amplifies mitochondrial and metabolic defenses. It mirrors the indirect resveratrol cascade, suggesting convergent circuitry among polyphenols.

subject: UBCS039
context: UBCS039 is the first synthetic, selective allosteric activator of SIRT6, binding its distal hydrophobic pocket and stimulating deacetylase activity (EC50 ≈ 38 μM). The directionality is UBCS039 binding SIRT6 to enhance its catalytic output. It preferentially engages the deacetylase function and drives chromatin compaction and tumor-suppressive programs. UBCS039 helped validate SIRT6 as a druggable longevity target.

subject: MDL-801
context: MDL-801 is a potent, cell-permeable synthetic allosteric activator of SIRT6 that binds the hydrophobic pocket and stimulates its deacetylase activity (EC50 ≈ 10.3 μM). The directionality is MDL-801 upstream of SIRT6 activation. It mirrors UBCS039 but with greater potency and cell permeability. MDL-801 mitigates kidney fibrosis and suppresses glycolytic, tumor-promoting metabolism.

subject: Cyanidin
context: Cyanidin, a natural anthocyanidin from red berries, increases SIRT6 activity by over 50-fold in certain in vitro assays, making it one of the most powerful natural SIRT6 activators. The directionality is cyanidin upstream of SIRT6 stimulation. Its potency suggests strong binding to the SIRT6 activation pocket. This links berry polyphenols to SIRT6-dependent metabolic and anti-aging effects.

subject: SIRT6
context: Activated SIRT6 rapidly deacetylates histone H3K9ac and H3K56ac at chromatin, promoting compaction and facilitating DNA-repair and silencing programs. The directionality is SIRT6 enzymatic removal of these active marks. Loss of H3K56ac in particular is associated with genome stability and stress resistance. This chromatin action underlies SIRT6's roles in longevity and tumor suppression.

subject: SIRT6
context: By suppressing glycolysis and pushing tumor cells toward oxidative metabolism or autophagy, SIRT6 activators such as UBCS039 display tumor-suppressive activity. The directionality is SIRT6 activation upstream of reduced Warburg glycolysis. This restrains the aerobic-glycolytic phenotype that fuels cancer growth. It is a mechanistic rationale for SIRT6 activation in oncology.

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 desuccinylates and activates carbamoyl phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1), the rate-limiting enzyme of the urea cycle, enhancing ammonia detoxification into urea. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of CPS1. This is especially important during fasting or high-protein load when nitrogen must be cleared. It exemplifies SIRT5's role as a regulator of mitochondrial acyl-metabolism.

subject: SIRT2 overactivity
context: Direct SIRT2 activation is generally avoided therapeutically because overactivity is linked to neurotoxicity in neurodegenerative contexts, where excessive deacetylation may impair microtubule and protein-homeostasis defenses. The directionality is SIRT2 overactivity associated with neuronal damage. Consequently, SIRT2 inhibitors are pursued for Parkinson's and Huntington's disease. This contrasts with most other sirtuins, where activation is sought.

subject: SIRT2 inhibitors (AGK2, AK-7, SirReal2)
context: Selective SIRT2 inhibitors such as AGK2, AK-7, and SirReal2 are investigated in neurodegenerative disease models because blocking SIRT2 preserves α-tubulin acetylation and protects neurons from aggregation toxicity. The directionality is SIRT2 inhibition → microtubule stability → neuroprotection. These agents rescue dopaminergic neurons from α-synuclein toxicity and confer ischemic protection. The approach exploits the inverse therapeutic logic of SIRT2 versus other sirtuins.

subject: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide)
context: NMN is a direct NAD+ precursor that, once converted to NAD+, serves as a universal indirect pan-sirtuin activator by supplying the obligate co-substrate for all seven sirtuins. The directionality is NMN → NAD+ → sirtuin activation. It raises NAD+ levels that decline with age, restoring sirtuin function systemically. NMN (with NR) is a leading nutraceutical strategy to counteract age-related sirtuin attenuation.

subject: NR (Nicotinamide Riboside)
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is an NAD+ precursor that raises cellular NAD+ and thereby indirectly activates all seven sirtuins by supplying their shared co-substrate. The directionality is NR → NAD+ → pan-sirtuin activation. Like NMN, NR reverses age-related NAD+ decline and restores sirtuin-dependent maintenance. It is a leading nutraceutical approach to broadly engage sirtuin biology.

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 is highly localized to the nucleolus and deacetylates histone H3K18 (H3K18ac), a mark associated with active rDNA transcription, thereby repressing ribosome biogenesis when deacetylated. The directionality is SIRT7 enzymatic removal of H3K18ac. Because excess ribosome production fuels growth and cancer, this repressive action can be tumor-suppressive in some contexts. It also stabilizes pericentric heterochromatin, supporting genome stability.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates the RelA/p65 subunit of NF-κB, particularly at Lys310, inhibiting its transcriptional activity and reducing expression of inflammatory genes. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatically inactivating NF-κB. This anti-inflammatory action is a cornerstone of SIRT1's protective effects in metabolic and cardiovascular disease. It complements SIRT1's promotion of p65 proteasomal degradation.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 inhibits NF-κB transcriptional activity by deacetylating the p65/RelA subunit at Lys310, preventing optimal promoter engagement. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of suppressed NF-κB signaling. This lowers chronic inflammation linked to aging and atherosclerosis. It is one of the best-established anti-inflammatory mechanisms of SIRT1.

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 at the promoters of NF-κB target genes, reducing their transcription and thereby dampening inflammation. The directionality is SIRT6 enzymatic chromatin repression of NF-κB-driven loci. This complements SIRT6's direct actions and underscores its anti-inflammatory role. Loss of SIRT6 elevates H3K9ac and inflammatory output.

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 overexpression suppresses NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses, as shown in models such as osteoarthritis development where cytokine production is reduced. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of inhibited NF-κB inflammation. This protection arises from both chromatin deacetylation and p65 degradation. It positions SIRT6 as a nuclear inflammation brake.

subject: SIRT1
context: Nuclear SIRT1 deacetylates RelA/p65, which licenses its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, lowering NF-κB levels and activity. The directionality is SIRT1 → p65 deacetylation → proteasomal turnover. Consequently, decreased SIRT1 raises NF-κB activity, while SIRT1 activation suppresses it. This degradation axis acts together with SIRT6 to constrain inflammation.

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 also deacetylates RelA/p65 and supports its proteasomal degradation, cooperating with SIRT1 to terminate NF-κB signaling. The directionality is SIRT6 → p65 destabilization → reduced NF-κB. Loss of either sirtuin elevates NF-κB activity, highlighting redundancy in this anti-inflammatory circuit. It is a key mechanism behind SIRT6's Anti-inflammatory and anti-aging effects.

subject: SIRT7
context: Knockdown of SIRT7 promotes nuclear translocation of NF-κB p-p65 and increases downstream inflammatory cytokines, whereas SIRT7 overexpression has the opposite effect by retaining NF-κB cytoplasmically. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of blocked p65 nuclear entry. This reveals a non-canonical, deacetylation-independent mode of NF-κB control by SIRT7. It ties SIRT7 to tissue inflammation, including in kidney.

subject: SIRT7-kidney-specific knockout
context: Kidney-specific SIRT7 knockout mice show diminished inflammation with reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 and suppressed nuclear NF-κB p65 accumulation, indicating SIRT7 normally promotes renal NF-κB activation. The directionality is SIRT7 loss → less nuclear p65 → lower inflammation. This is somewhat counterintuitive given SIRT7's usual anti-inflammatory renal role elsewhere, underscoring context dependence. It suggests SIRT7 can be pro-inflammatory in specific renal settings.
